name: Anger

counsel.text: Rise mightily against the first actings of thy distemper, its first conceptions; suffer it not to get the least ground. Do not say, "Thus far it shall go, and no farther." If it have allowance for one step, it will take another. It is impossible to fix bounds to sin. It is like water in a channel, -- if it once break out, it will have its course.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: Some man is never so much troubled all his life, perhaps, with anger and passion, nor doth trouble others, as another is almost every day; and yet the latter hath done more to the mortification of the sin than the former.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 5

counsel.text: Ought not all our expectations to this purpose to be on Christ alone? Let this, then, be fixed upon thy heart, that if thou hast not relief from him thou shalt never have any.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: Seeing we have so little power over our hearts when once they meet with suitable provocations, we are to keep them asunder, as a man would do fire and the combustible parts of the house wherein he dwells.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: True, anger is good when mixed with holy zeal. Anger is without sin when it is against sin: but to sin in anger, to speak unadvisedly with the lips, is to have the tongue set on fire of hell.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the third commandment

counsel.text: How much have you heard against rash anger, that is a short frenzy, a dry drunkenness; that it rests in the bosom of fools; and upon the least occasion do your spirits begin to take fire?
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Art of Divine Contentment, ch. 2

counsel.text: Is it not irrational to gratify an enemy? In sin we do so. When lust or rash anger burns in the soul, Satan warms himself at this fire. Men's sins feast the devil.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson

counsel.text: Let us, therefore, when any lawless passions begin to stir, deal with our souls as God did with Jonah, 'Doest thou well to be angry?' Jonah 4. 4, to fret thus. This will be a means to make us quiet; for, alas! what weak reasons have we often of strong motions.
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 5

counsel.text: It is a holy state of soul to be under the power of nothing beneath itself. Are we stirred? then consider, is this matter worth the loss of my quiet?
counsel.author: Richard Sibbes
counsel.source: The Soul's Conflict with Itself, ch. 10

counsel.text: Sometimes good men are sick of the frets, but when they are, it costs them dear, as Job and Jonah found by experience. No man hath ever got anything by his fretting and flinging, except it hath been harder blows or heavier chains; therefore fret not when God strikes.
counsel.author: Thomas Brooks
counsel.source: The Mute Christian Under the Smarting Rod

counsel.text: Fighting with men and storming of castles is but children's play to this encounter, where devils and lusts are to be repelled. 'He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty; and he that ruleth his spirit than he that taketh a city,' Prov. 16:32. 'Better,' because he overcomes a worse enemy, infinitely more potent and puissant.
counsel.author: William Gurnall

counsel.text: When thou art raging in thy passion, throwing burning coals of wrath and fury about with thy inflamed tongue, where was it set on fire, but of hell?
counsel.author: William Gurnall

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Righteous and patient Father, you are slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love, and you have borne with me far longer than I have borne with anyone. I come to you in the name of Jesus Christ, my only Mediator. I confess that I have been sinfully angry. I have raised my voice, spoken sharp words, and nursed hard thoughts until they turned into malice. Beneath my anger I find a proud heart that demands its own way and treats my wishes as if they were your law. When others crossed me, I set myself up as their judge, forgetting that I too must stand before you. My anger has not produced your righteousness. It has wounded the people you gave me to love, and it has grieved your Holy Spirit. I do not only want to be rid of the trouble it brings me; teach me to hate it because it is against you. Forgive me for the sake of Christ, who bore your righteous anger in my place, and who did not revile when he was reviled. Holy Spirit, put this anger to death at its root, and give me grace to seek the forgiveness of those I have hurt. I thank you that your wrath against me was poured out on your Son, and none is left for me. In his name. Amen.

prayers.title: When anger rises
prayers.text: Lord, my heart is hot within me, and I am ready to say what I will regret. Stop me before the first word. Set a guard over my mouth and keep watch at the door of my lips. Do not let me feed this anger, even in my thoughts; help me put it down now, while it is small. Remind me how much you have forgiven me, and how patiently you bear with me every day. Lord Jesus, when you suffered you did not threaten, but entrusted yourself to him who judges justly. Teach me to leave this in your hands. Holy Spirit, quiet my heart, and give me a soft answer that turns away wrath. Amen.

prayers.title: For a gentle spirit
prayers.text: Father, your Son is gentle and lowly in heart, and you have called me to be like him. Search me and show me what lies under my anger: the pride that must be right, the fear of losing control, the demand for my own comfort. Pull it up by the roots. Clothe me with compassion, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience. When I am wronged, teach me to look first at my own sin, then at your cross, and only then at the wrong done to me. Make me a peacemaker in my home and in my church, so that people find it easy to come near me. For Christ's sake. Amen.

prayers.title: Confessing passion and rash anger
prayers.text: We have not had the rule which we ought to have had over our own spirits, which have therefore been as a city that is broken down, and has no walls. We have been soon angry, and anger hath rested in our bosoms. And when our spirits have been provoked, we have spoken unadvisedly with our lips; and have been guilty of that clamour and bitterness which should have been put far from us.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

prayers.title: That anger may never rest in us
prayers.text: Let anger never rest in our bosoms, nor the sun ever go down upon our wrath; but enable us to show all meekness towards all men, because we ourselves also were sometimes foolish and disobedient. Let us be clothed as becomes the elect of God, holy and beloved, with bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, and long-suffering; that being merciful as our Father which is in heaven is merciful, we may be perfect as he is perfect.
prayers.author: Matthew Henry

examinationQuestions: When your anger rose today, what did you want that you were not getting: respect, control, comfort, or your own way?
What were the occasions of your anger, such as hurry, weariness, a certain person, or a certain subject, and did you see it coming before it broke out?
Was your anger for God's honor and against sin, or for your own honor and against someone who crossed you?
Is there anyone you have wounded with your words or your silence whom you have not yet gone to and asked forgiveness?
Do you excuse your temper as just the way you are made? How would you see it if you counted it as sin that Christ had to die for?
God has been patient with you today. How should his patience shape the way you treat those who try yours?
fleeActions: Stop talking now. Say only, "I need a few minutes," and quietly leave the room before you say more.
Go outside and walk until your breathing slows. Pray as you walk, and tell the Lord honestly what you feel.
Do not send that message, email, or post. Put the phone down and wait until you have prayed and slept on it.
Open your Bible and read Psalm 37:1-11 or James 1:19-21 slowly, out loud if you can.
Ask one of your brethren to pray for you, and tell them honestly that you are angry. If your anger has ever frightened or harmed someone, speak to your pastor this week and get help.
When your heart is quiet, go back to the one you hurt and ask forgiveness plainly, without excuses.

afterFallReadings.text: Let us all set upon this great work of repentance; let us repent sincerely and speedily: let us repent of all our sins, our pride, rash anger, and unbelief.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson

afterFallReadings.text: When the widow brought empty vessels to Elisha, the oil was poured into them. 2 Kings 4: 6. Bring God the broken vessel of a contrite heart, and he will pour in the oil of mercy.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson

afterFallReadings.text: Yea, let me add, that never any soul did or shall perish by the power of any lust, sin, or corruption, who could raise his soul by faith to an expectation of relief from Jesus Christ.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14
